src/domain/models.ts: User, Task and Project are related domain entities linked through `assigneeId`, `projectId` and `tasks: Task[]`.
src/domain/models.ts: `Repository { projects: Map<string, Project>; users: Map<string, User>; }` is a collection of the same entities in the same file.
Task-to-project membership is stored twice, as `Task.projectId` and `Project.tasks`. This is a minor overlap between data shapes, not duplicated rule logic.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit has one file, src/domain/models.ts, and it covers one concern: the domain data model for a task-tracking system. It declares TaskStatus, User, Task, Project and Repository. TaskStatus is defined once and Task.status reuses it, so the allowed status values live in one place. No file splits the unit into unrelated concerns, and nothing works around the module's own types, since they are all plain type declarations. There are two minor points, but neither is serious enough to fail the unit. First, the Project–Task relationship is stored in both directions: Task has a projectId field and Project has a tasks array. That means two places record which project a task belongs to, but these are data shapes, not duplicated rule logic. Second, Repository is described as concrete in-memory Maps rather than as an abstract port. That is a modelling choice inside the same file, not a split into separate concerns.
